about: Reachable: an open security group on a listener port, a public instance open on 80 (argus_v10), an NLB without security groups, a function URL without auth, an EKS endpoint open to anywhere. In a VPC (ADR-0035, second amendment) every resource sits in a subnet with a route table and a network ACL: no route to an internet gateway, an ACL that denies the port or the reply, an IPv6 rule on an IPv4-only instance are restricted; a dual-stack ALB and an instance open only over IPv6 are open per family; a route table, ACL, security group or subnet missing from the inventory is unknown (internet-unverified). The same estate for internet-entry, internet-restricted and internet-unverified: each candidate is in exactly one of them, and DNS records, private APIs, internal or stopped resources in none. An Elastic IP on an instance's second network interface is a public address; that interface's groups decide. Added 2026-10-21 (ADR-0035, fourth amendment): a UDP listener matches a UDP rule (dns, open) and a TCP listener does not (dns-tcp, restricted); a default route to a firewall endpoint (vpce-) is unknown (i-fw); an instance with no public address is restricted when a group opens it to the internet (i-private) and no door otherwise (i-quiet). Restricted rows name open_ports, listens and default_routes. Added 2026-10-21 (ADR-0035, fifth amendment): a stopped instance whose group opens a port is restricted (i-stopped, not_running), one whose groups open nothing (i-stopclosed) and a terminated one (i-terminated) are no door; an ICMP-only group opens nothing (i-icmp); an instance is judged per network interface, so an open group on its private interface and a closed one on its public interface are restricted (i-twoeni, no_public_address). Every VPC door carries `network` (per interface: public families, open per family, each subnet's route and ACL) and an instance its `state`. Public by their own policy (version bump, ADR-0037 second amendment): a bucket allowing * (open), one with Block Public Access restricting public buckets (restricted), one whose account's S3 settings are not in the inventory and a queue whose public statement has a condition (unknown), a queue open to anyone. Near misses: a function's InvokeFunctionUrl to * (its URL's), a service principal, a Deny, the account's own root. Version bump (wave 3): an instance's metadata service as `imds` (v1 when tokens are optional, v2 when required).
